data.title: STOCKS | Meta-Tied Data Center’s First Junk Bond Draws More Than Four Times Demand
data.description:
The first junk-bond offering for a data center tied to Meta Platforms Inc. drew demand more than four times the deal’s size, according to Bloomberg.

Investors were attracted by the bond’s juicy yields.

data.title: Trump Crypto Ties Draw Scrutiny After CLARITY Act Fails Senate Vote
data.description:
The CLARITY Act failed to secure the 60 votes needed to advance in the Senate on Tuesday, renewing scrutiny of U.S. President Donald Trump’s crypto ventures. According to NS3.AI, industry figures said Trump’s financial ties and family businesses turned the legislation into a debate over presidential ethics, while the White House blamed Democrats.

The bill’s defeat also prompted warnings about possible consequences for U.S. crypto policy and the country’s competitiveness.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Haworth Says Oil Is Driving Higher Rates
data.description:
Treasuries fell as traders anticipated additional Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes and increased wagers on rising yields for short-maturity debt, according to Bloomberg.

Rob Haworth, senior investment strategy director at U.S. Bank Asset Management, said oil is driving rates higher on Bloomberg Businessweek Daily.

data.title: Europe Refiners Face Higher Premiums After Saudi Pipeline Attack Cuts Sales
data.description:
Europe’s oil refiners are paying steep premiums for cargoes after the shutdown of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline forced buyers to seek alternatives, according to Bloomberg.

Fuel prices have also surged.

data.title: Kevin O'Leary Says Bitcoin Could Reach $1 Million If Quantum Risk Is Resolved
data.description:
Kevin O'Leary said Bitcoin could reach $1 million if the industry resolves concerns that quantum computers could eventually break the encryption securing the network. According to NS3.AI, he said institutions may continue treating Bitcoin as a novelty rather than a core holding until that risk is addressed.

O'Leary also discussed tokenized stocks, blockchain adoption, AI-related power demand, and his investments in uranium and power infrastructure.

data.title: DCC Energy Shareholders Back KKR, ECP’s £5.7 Billion Takeover
data.description:
DCC Energy Plc shareholders approved a takeover by KKR & Co. and Energy Capital Partners valued at more than £5.7 billion ($7.6 billion), according to Bloomberg.

The deal follows a drawn-out pursuit of the energy distributor.

data.title: Muni Funds See $1.8 Billion Outflow as Return Slump Continues
data.description: Investors pulled about $1.8 billion from the municipal bond market this week as returns for state and local government debt were on track to fall for a third straight month, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI | Nvidia, Google and Emerald AI Launch AI Energy Management Alliance
data.description:
Nvidia, Google and Emerald AI have formed the AI Energy Management Alliance to dynamically manage data center electricity use based on grid conditions, according to Bloomberg.

Varun Sivaram, founder and CEO of Emerald AI, joins to discuss the alliance.

data.title: Meltem Demirors Says Bitcoin Infrastructure Is Helping Drive AI
data.description:
Meltem Demirors said Bitcoin helped build infrastructure that is now supporting artificial intelligence, but she argued that the technology’s ultimate output was not the one she would have chosen. According to NS3.AI, she said crypto companies and miners have brought energy and computing expertise into AI, while the shift by miners toward AI and high-performance computing raises a legitimate concern for Bitcoin’s security.

Demirors added that Bitcoin’s difficulty adjustment can help the network adapt as computing power moves elsewhere.

data.title: Municipal Bonds Draw Investors as Treasury Yields Rise
data.description:
According to CNBC, municipal bonds are offering more attractive tax-exempt income opportunities as the Federal Reserve keeps raising interest rates and Treasury yields remain elevated, with the 10-year Treasury reaching 5% on Friday. The Bloomberg Municipal Bond Index is yielding about 4.3%, while Chris Gunster, head of fixed income at Fidelis Capital, said that translates to a 7.3% tax-equivalent yield for investors in the highest tax bracket. The iShares National Muni Bond ETF (MUB) has a 30-day SEC yield of 3.8% and an expense ratio of 0.05%.

Bank of America strategist Yingchen Li said the muni market is waiting for stability in Treasurys after the yield curve flattened sharply this week, and said the Fed's firmer stance plus Treasury buybacks of long bonds should support munis. The Treasury Department said last week it will buy back up to $6 billion in longer-term debt. Barclays also said it is adding exposure to municipals, with Mikhail Foux saying muni ratios have widened, index yields are near multi-year highs and investors should gradually add higher-quality names.

data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, WTI October crude oil futures settled at $100.30 a barrel, NYMEX October natural gas futures settled at $2.9120 per million British thermal units, NYMEX October gasoline futures settled at $3.5276 a gallon, and NYMEX October heating oil futures settled at $5.0578 a gallon.

data.title: STOCKS | Global Cross-Border Commercial Real Estate Investment Rises 56% in First Half
data.description:
Global cross-border commercial real estate investment rose 56% year on year to $71.8 billion in the first half of 2026, according to research data. According to Sina Finance, that was well above about $46 billion in the same period last year.

Europe attracted $39.9 billion, while Asia drew $19.3 billion, and the two regions together accounted for more than 82% of global cross-border investment. By destination, Europe accounted for about 55.6% of the global total, while Asia made up about 26.9%.

Outside Europe and Asia, other regions received about $12.6 billion in cross-border investment. The report said cross-border investment refers to investors buying real estate assets in markets outside their place of registration.

A survey of European investors at the start of the year showed 89% expected real estate buying activity to increase or remain stable in 2026. London remained the most closely watched cross-border investment city in Europe, followed by Madrid, Warsaw, Barcelona and Milan.

In Asia, cross-border commercial real estate investment appetite also improved. The region attracted $19.3 billion in cross-border funds in the first half, and more than 57% of respondents said they planned to increase real estate investment in 2026.

Office properties became the most preferred commercial real estate category among Asian investors for the first time in six years, followed by industrial and logistics facilities, living assets and data centers. Tokyo was ranked the most favored cross-border investment destination in Asia for the seventh consecutive year, followed by Sydney, with Singapore and Seoul tied for third.

Global direct real estate investment rose 28% year on year in the second quarter, with investment up 38% in Asia-Pacific, 27% in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and 26% in the Americas. The report said financing costs could still limit transaction speed in the second half.

data.title: Westinghouse Seeks More Than $50 Billion Valuation in US IPO
data.description:
Westinghouse Electric Co. is targeting a valuation of more than $50 billion in its US initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, Bloomberg reported.

The company provides reactor technology to nuclear power plants.

data.title: SpaceX Expands NASA Contract With Three More Crew Flights Through 2030
data.description: According to CNBC, SpaceX has expanded its contract with NASA and will carry out three additional crewed Dragon flights to the International Space Station through 2030, with the work worth up to $946 million if completed. The award lifts SpaceX's total missions under NASA's Commercial Crew Transportation Capability contract to 17 operational flights, and NASA said the deal helps it maintain access to the station with two commercial crew providers. SpaceX will handle ground, launch, in-orbit, cargo transport, and return and recovery operations, along with lifeboat capability while docked to the ISS. Under the contract, SpaceX will have earned $5.92 billion from NASA. NASA said Crew 13 is expected to launch in October and Crew 14 is slated for next spring.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Canada’s Joly Urges Stellantis and Union to Resume Labor Talks
data.description:
Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly urged Stellantis NV and its unionized workers to resume labor talks on Friday, according to Bloomberg.

Stellantis is the parent of Jeep.

data.title: AI TRENDS | FDA Approves Inluriyo Imlunestrant for Use With Verzenio
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Inluriyo Imlunestrant for use in combination with Verzenio.

data.title: STOCKS | ICE Brent crude net longs rise to 282,657 contracts, a 17-week high
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, speculators' net long positions in ICE Brent crude rose by 16,904 contracts to 282,657 in the week of September 15, a 17-week high.

data.title: Pentagon Tells Congress U.S. Iran-Related Spending Has Reached $43.6 Billion
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the Pentagon told Congress that U.S. spending on Iran-related operations has reached $43.6 billion so far, including about $11.2 billion for incremental operation costs, about $28.1 billion to replenish expended munitions, and about $4.3 billion to replace lost equipment.

data.title: STOCKS | AAII Sentiment Falls to 16-Month Low
data.description:
Investor sentiment dropped to its lowest level in 16 months, according to Bloomberg, as the American Association of Individual Investors' weekly survey showed.

Oil prices stayed elevated while the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023.

data.title: STOCKS | UBS's Lovell Says Earnings, Not Fed, Are Driving Stocks
data.description:
Nadia Lovell, head of global equity strategy at UBS Global Wealth Management, said strong earnings and broadening profit growth should keep stocks moving higher even as rising rates create near-term volatility, according to Bloomberg.

Speaking on "Bloomberg Surveillance," Lovell said earnings, not valuation expansion, will drive the market.
